title: Bekhorot 46
description: The blemishes chapter closes with vows the public must consent to, and a new chapter opens: who counts as a firstborn for the double share of inheritance, who for the five sela’im paid to the priest, and how much of a baby must emerge for its birth to count.

a2.he: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר: הִלְכְתָא, אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר נֶדֶר שֶׁהוּדַּר בָּרַבִּים יֵשׁ לוֹ הֲפָרָה, עַל דַּעַת הָרַבִּים אֵין לוֹ הֲפָרָה. וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי לִדְבַר הָרְשׁוּת, אֲבָל לִדְבַר מִצְוָה יֵשׁ לוֹ הֲפָרָה. כִּי הָהוּא דְּמַקְרֵי דַרְדְּקֵי, אַדְּרֵיהּ רַב אַחָא דְּקָא פָשַׁע בְּיָנוֹקֵי, וְאַהְדְּרֵיהּ רָבִינָא, דְּלָא אַשְׁכַּח דַּהֲוָה דָּיֵיק כְּוָותֵיהּ.

a3.he: וְהַמִּטַּמֵּא לְמֵתִים כּוּ׳. מַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דְּסַגִּי לֵיהּ בְּקַבָּלָה, וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָתָם דְּמַדְּרִינַן לֵיהּ? הָתָם יִצְרוֹ תְּקָפוֹ.

a5.he: מַתְנִי׳ יֵשׁ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה, וְאֵינוֹ בְּכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן; בְּכוֹר לִכְהֵן, וְאֵינוֹ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה; בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה וְלַכֹּהֵן, וְיֵשׁ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּכוֹר לֹא לַנַּחֲלָה וְלֹא לַכֹּהֵן.

a6.he: אֵיזֶהוּ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה וְאֵינוֹ בְּכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן? הַבָּא אַחַר נְפָלִים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיָּצָא אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ חַי, וּבֶן תִּשְׁעָה שֶׁיָּצָא רֹאשׁוֹ מֵת, הַמַּפֶּלֶת כְּמִין בְּהֵמָה חַיָּה וָעוֹף — דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.

a7.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ מִצּוּרַת אָדָם. הַמַּפֶּלֶת סַנְדָּל, אוֹ שִׁלְיָא, אוֹ שַׁפִּיר מְרוּקָּם, וְהַיּוֹצֵא מְחוּתָּךְ — הַבָּא אַחֲרֵיהֶם בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה, וְאֵין בְּכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן.

a8.he: מִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים, וְנָשָׂא אִשָּׁה שֶׁכְּבָר יָלְדָה, עוֹדָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְנִשְׁתַּחְרְרָה, עוֹדָהּ נׇכְרִית וְנִתְגַּיְּירָה, מִשֶּׁבָּאת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל יָלְדָה — בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה וְאֵין בְּכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן.

a9.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה וְלַכֹּהֵן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״ — עַד שֶׁיִּפְטְרוּ רֶחֶם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.

a10.he: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים וְנָשָׂא אִשָּׁה שֶׁלֹּא יָלְדָה, נִתְגַּיְּירָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת, נִשְׁתַּחְרְרָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת.

a11.he: וְיָלְדָה הִיא וְכֹהֶנֶת הִיא, וּלְוִיָּה הִיא, וְאִשָּׁה שֶׁכְּבָר יָלְדָה, וְכֵן מִי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁהֲתָה לְאַחַר בַּעְלָהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים וְנִשֵּׂאת וְיָלְדָה, וְאֵינוֹ יָדוּעַ אִם בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה לָרִאשׁוֹן אִם בִּן שִׁבְעָה לָאַחֲרוֹן — בְּכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן וְאֵינוֹ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה.

b1.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֵין הָרֹאשׁ פּוֹטֵר בִּנְפָלִים.

b2.he: מַאי טַעְמָא? ״כֹּל אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁמַת רוּחַ חַיִּים בְּאַפָּיו״ — כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּנִשְׁמַת רוּחַ חַיִּים בְּאַפָּיו הוּא דַּחֲשִׁיב רֵישֵׁיהּ, אִידַּךְ לָא חֲשִׁיב רֵישֵׁיהּ.

b3.he: תְּנַן: הַבָּא אַחַר נְפָלִים, שֶׁיָּצָא רֹאשׁוֹ חַי, וּבֶן תִּשְׁעָה שֶׁיָּצָא רֹאשׁוֹ מֵת. קָתָנֵי מִיהָא ״רֹאשׁוֹ!״ מַאי ״רֹאשׁוֹ?״ רוּבּוֹ.

b4.he: וְלִיתְנֵי ״רוּבּוֹ״! בְּדִין הוּא דְּאִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְמִיתְנֵי רוּבּוֹ, וְאַיְּידֵי דְּקָא בָעֵי לְמִיתְנֵי סֵיפָא בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה שֶׁיָּצָא רֹאשׁוֹ מֵת — טַעְמָא דְּרֹאשׁוֹ מֵת, הָא רֹאשׁוֹ חַי — הַבָּא אַחֲרָיו בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה נָמֵי לָא הָוֵי, תְּנָא רֵישָׁא נָמֵי רֹאשׁוֹ.

b5.he: וּמַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, דְּכֵיוָן דְּמַפֵּיק לֵיהּ רֵישֵׁיהּ הָוֵה [לֵיהּ] לֵידָה? תְּנֵינָא: הוֹצִיא רֹאשׁוֹ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֶחְזִירוֹ — הֲרֵי זֶה כְּיָלוּד!

b6.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן בְּהֵמָה, וְקָא מַשְׁמַע לַן בְּאָדָם, דְּאָדָם מִבְּהֵמָה לָא יָלֵיף — דְּלֵית לַהּ פְּרוֹזְדוֹר.

b7.he: בְּהֵמָה מֵאָדָם לָא יָלְפָא — מִשּׁוּם דַּחֲשִׁיב פַּרְצוּף פָּנִים דִּידֵיהּ.

b8.he: הָא נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא: יָצָא כְּדַרְכּוֹ — מִשֶּׁיָּצָא רוֹב רֹאשׁוֹ, וְאֵיזֶהוּ רוֹב רֹאשׁוֹ? מִשֶּׁתֵּצֵא פַּדַּחְתּוֹ. תְּיוּבְתָּא דִשְׁמוּאֵל, תְּיוּבְתָּא!

b9.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: פַּדַּחַת פּוֹטֶרֶת בְּכׇל מָקוֹם, חוּץ מִן הַנַּחֲלָה. מַאי טַעְמָא? ״יַכִּיר״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ לַנַּחֲלָה.

b10.he: בְּכׇל מָקוֹם, לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵיתוֹיֵי הָא דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: גִּיּוֹרֶת שֶׁיָּצְאָה פַּדַּחַת וְלָדָהּ בְּגַיּוּתָהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְגַּיְּירָה — אֵין נוֹתְנִין לָהּ יְמֵי טוּמְאָה וִימֵי טׇהֳרָה, וְאֵינָהּ מְבִיאָה קׇרְבַּן לֵידָה.

b11.he: מֵיתִיבִי: ״יַכִּיר״ — זוֹ הַכָּרַת פָּנִים, וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא הַכָּרַת פָּנִים? פַּרְצוּף פָּנִים עִם הַחוֹטֶם. תָּנֵי: ״עַד הַחוֹטֶם״. תָּא שְׁמַע: אֵין מְעִידִים אֶלָּא עַל פַּרְצוּף פָּנִים עִם הַחוֹטֶם. תְּנִי: ״עַד הַחוֹטֶם״.

b12.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: פַּדַּחַת בְּלֹא פַּרְצוּף פָּנִים, פַּרְצוּף פָּנִים בְּלֹא פַּדַּחַת — אֵין מְעִידִין עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם עִם הַחוֹטֶם. וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב כָּהֲנָא: מַאי קְרָאָה? ״הַכָּרַת פְּנֵיהֶם עָנְתָה בָּם״! שָׁאנֵי עֵדוּת אִשָּׁה, דְּאַחְמִירוּ בַּהּ רַבָּנַן.

b13.he: וּמִי אַחְמִירוּ? וְהָא תְּנַן: הוּחְזְקוּ לִהְיוֹת מַשִּׂיאִים עֵד מִפִּי עֵד, מִפִּי אִשָּׁה, מִפִּי עֶבֶד, מִפִּי שִׁפְחָה! כִּי אַקִּילוּ רַבָּנַן בְּסוֹפָהּ, בִּתְחִלָּתָהּ לָא אַקִּילוּ רַבָּנַן.

messages.text: Continued from 45b: a priest who married a woman forbidden to him must vow not to benefit from her. The Gemara asked how that vow is kept from being dissolved, even by those who hold that a vow taken in public can be nullified, and answers that we administer the vow…
…to the priest based on the consent of the public, making it a type of vow that cannot be dissolved without their consent.

The halakha is as follows: Even according to the one who says a vow that was taken in public has the option of nullification, if it was taken based on the consent of the public it has no option of nullification.

notes.dh: אמר אמימר הלכתא אפי' למ"ד כו'
notes.he: בפ' השולח (בגיטין לו.) גרס הלכתא אפי' למ"ד כו' ובמכות (דף טז.) גרסי' ברוב ספרים הלכתא נדר שהודר ברבים יש לו הפרה ולמאי דגרסי' נמי אפי' למ"ד נדר שהודר ברבים שלא בא עכשיו לפסוק בהודר ברבים מ"מ יש לדקדק מדהוצרך לפסוק אין לו הפרה בעל דעת רבים לכ"ע מכלל שסבר דברבים יש לו הפרה דאי אין לו הפרה כל שכן בעל דעת רבים ושלא בלשון פסק היה לו לומר אפי' למ"ד ואע"ג דאסקינן בפ' השולח (גיטין דף לה:) אליבא דרב נחמן דמדרינן ליה ברבים דמשמע דס"ל הכי דקי"ל כוותיה בדיני ולענין דינא איתשיל הא פריך בתר הכי הניחא למ"ד כו' ולאו אמתניתין דפרקין דמייתי התם לחודיה קאי אלא קאי נמי אדרב נחמן מדאדריה נמי רב אחא לההוא מקרי דרדקי על דעת רבים משמע דקסבר דברבים יש לו הפרה דלא מיסתבר לומר דלכך הוצרך על דעת רבים ולא אמר הדירו ברבים לפי שלא היו רבים מזומנים לפניו ורב יוסף דאמר בערבי פסחים (פסחים קז.) (אמר) [אדור] ברבים דלא אשתי שכרא משמע דקסבר דברבים אין לו הפרה לא קי"ל הכי:
notes.en: Ameimar says: The halakha is, even according to the one who says, etc.: In chapter HaSholeaḥ (Gittin 36a) the reading is “The halakha is: even according to the one who says…”, and in Makkot (16a) most books read: “The halakha is: a vow taken in public can be nullified.” And even on our reading, “even according to the one who says a vow taken in public…”, so that he is not coming now to rule about a vow taken in public, one can still infer something: since he needed to rule that a vow on the consent of the public cannot be nullified according to everyone, it follows that he holds a vow taken in public can be nullified. For if it could not be nullified, all the more so one on the consent of the public, and he should have said “even according to the one who says” without the language of a ruling. And although in chapter HaSholeaḥ (Gittin 35b) we conclude, according to Rav Naḥman, that we administer the vow to him in public, which implies that he holds so, and we rule like him in civil law, and the question there was asked about practical law, still it objects after that: “This works out well according to the one who says, etc.”, and that refers not only to the mishna of our chapter cited there but also to Rav Naḥman. And since Rav Aḥa too administered the vow to that teacher of children on the consent of the public, this implies that he holds a vow in public can be nullified; for it is not reasonable to say that he needed “on the consent of the public”, and did not administer the vow in public, only because there was no public gathered before him. And as for Rav Yosef, who said in Arvei Pesaḥim (Pesaḥim 107a), “[I was put under a vow] in public not to drink beer”, implying that he holds a vow in public cannot be nullified: we do not hold so.

messages.text: And this matter applies only to when the nullification of a vow is in order to enable one to perform an optional matter, but to enable one to perform a matter of a mitzva it has the option of nullification.
messages.quote: on the consent of the public it has no option of nullification

notes.he: דאין לו הפרה לנדר שהודר על דעת רבים:
notes.en: And this matter applies: that a vow taken on the consent of the public has no nullification.

notes.dh: אבל לדבר מצוה יש לו הפרה
notes.he: אומר ר"ת דמשום דמסתמא ניחא להו לרבים ועוד אמר ר"ת דעל דעת [רבים] היינו כשמפרש על דעת פלוני ופלוני ואפילו שלא בפניהם אבל על דעת [רבים] סתם לאו כלום הוא ועל דעת יחיד ואע"פ שפירש על דעתו יכול חכם להתיר:
notes.en: But for a matter of a mitzva it can be nullified: Rabbeinu Tam says: because presumably the public is content [with that]. And Rabbeinu Tam further said: “on the consent of the public” means when he specifies “on the consent of So-and-so and So-and-so”, even not in their presence; but “on the consent of the public” without specifying is nothing. And [a vow] on the consent of an individual, even if he specified him by name, a Sage can release.

messages.text: As in the incident involving a certain teacher of children, upon whom Rav Aḥa administered a vow to cease teaching based on the consent of the public, as he was negligent with regard to the children by hitting them too much;

notes.he: שלא ילמד עוד תינוקות:
notes.en: Upon whom Rav Aḥa administered a vow: that he would no longer teach children.

notes.he: מלקה אותן ומתים:
notes.en: He was negligent with the children: he would beat them, and they would die. [So Rashi’s printed text reads; the Gemara itself says only that he hit them too much.]

notes.he: אדעתא דרבים:
notes.en: Upon whom Rav Aḥa administered a vow: on the consent of the public.

messages.text: and Ravina had his vow nullified and reinstated him, as they did not find another teacher who was as meticulous as he was.

What is different here that it is sufficient for him merely to accept upon himself a commitment in order to continue serving in the Temple, and what is different there, where the priest marries by a transgression, that we administer a vow to him?
messages.lead: § The mishna teaches that a priest who becomes impure through exposure to corpses is disqualified from performing the Temple service until he accepts upon himself that he will no longer become impure in that manner.

messages.text: There his desire seizes him, and it is therefore necessary for the priest to take a vow.

notes.he:
בלא נדר:
גבי נשים יצרו תוקפו להכי מדרינן ליה:
notes.en: By acceptance: without a vow. With regard to [forbidden] women, his inclination overpowers him; therefore we administer a vow to him.

notes.he: התם בנושא נשים בעבירה אימר יצרו תוקפו דנשאה ואי לא מדיר ודאי לא מגרש:
notes.en: There, with one who marries women by a transgression, say that his inclination overpowers him [toward] marrying her; and if we did not administer a vow to him, he certainly would not divorce [her].

notes.he: סליק פירקא
notes.en: The chapter is concluded.

messages.text: Hadran alakh Mumin Elu: we will return to you, chapter 7, “These Blemishes.”
Chapter 8 · יש בכור לנחלה · Yesh Bekhor LeNaḥala: the firstborn for inheritance and the firstborn for the priest.
Mishna

There is a son who is a firstborn with regard to inheritance but is not a firstborn with regard to the requirement of redemption from a priest. There is another who is a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest but is not a firstborn with regard to inheritance.

notes.he: ליטול פי שנים:
notes.en: MISHNA: There is a firstborn for inheritance: to take a double portion.

notes.he: לתת לכהן פדיונו ה' סלעים:
notes.en: For the priest: to give the priest his redemption, five sela’im.

notes.dh: מתני' יש בכור לנחלה כו' איזהו בכור לנחלה כו'
notes.he: הכא נקיט אמאי דפתח ביה וזימנין דנקט אדסליק מיניה כדמפרש בריש נדרים (דף ב:):
notes.en: MISHNA: There is a firstborn for inheritance, etc. Which is a firstborn for inheritance, etc.: here [the mishna] takes up first the case it opened with, and sometimes it takes up the case it ended with, as is explained at the beginning of Nedarim (2b).

messages.text: There is another who is a firstborn with regard to inheritance and with regard to redemption from a priest. And there is another who is not a firstborn at all, neither with regard to inheritance nor with regard to redemption from a priest.

Which is the son who is a firstborn with regard to inheritance but is not a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest? It is a son who came after miscarriage of an underdeveloped fetus, even where the head of the underdeveloped fetus emerged alive; or after a fully developed nine-month-old fetus whose head emerged dead.

notes.he: שיצא ראשו של נפל חי כגון שהיו תאומים אחד נפל ואחד כלו לו חדשיו והוציא נפל ראשו חי והחזירו ובא חבירו וקדמו ויצא זה האחרון בכור לנחלה דראשון לא הפסידו ואע"ג דראשו שהוציא חשוב לידה מעליא מ"ט דגבי נחלה כתיב ראשית אונו מי שלב אביו דוה עליו אם מת יצא נפל שהוציא ראשו ראשון והוי כילוד דלאו בר קיימא הוא ואין לבו דוה עליו אבל לענין כהן פטור האי ולד אחרון דבפטר רחם תליא מילתא והרי ראשון פטר את הרחם:
notes.en: One who comes after nonviable fetuses, even though the head of the nonviable fetus emerged alive: for example, there were twins, one a nonviable fetus [nefel] and the other full-term. The nefel put out its head alive and drew it back, and its brother came ahead of it and was born. This latter child is a firstborn for inheritance, since the first did not cause him to lose it. And although the head it put out counts as a proper birth, why [is he still a firstborn for inheritance]? Because with regard to inheritance it is written “the first of his strength” (Deuteronomy 21:17): one over whom his father’s heart would grieve if he died. Here a nefel came out and put its head out first, and it counts as born, but it is not viable, and his heart does not grieve over it. But with regard to the priest, this later child is exempt, since that matter depends on opening the womb, and the first one opened the womb.

notes.he: והחזירו ויצא אחיו הוי בכור לנחלה דהא ראשון לא חשיב שאין הלב [אביו] דוה עליו ולענין כהן פטר רחם הוא אבל יצא ראשון בן ט' חי ואח"כ החזירו ומת בכור לנחלה נמי לא הוי זה הבא אחריו:
notes.en: And a nine-month-old whose head emerged dead: and it drew it back, and its brother came out. [The brother] is a firstborn for inheritance, since the first does not count, as [his father’s] heart does not grieve over it; and with regard to the priest, [the first] opened the womb. But if the nine-month-old [put its head out] first while alive, and afterward drew it back and died, the one who comes after it is not a firstborn even for inheritance.

notes.he: הבא אחר הנפלים בני ח':
notes.en: One who comes after nonviable fetuses: eight-month-old ones.

notes.he: כיון דלאו בר קיימא הוי הבא אחריו בכור לנחלה הוי ולא בכור לכהן דלא הוי פטר רחם:
notes.en: And even though its head emerged alive: since it is not viable, the one who comes after it is a firstborn for inheritance; but he is not a firstborn for the priest, since he is not the one who opened the womb.

messages.text: The same applies to a son born to a woman who had previously miscarried a fetus that had the appearance of a type of domesticated animal, undomesticated animal, or bird, as that is considered the opening of the womb. This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: למיפטר מנחלה לא חשיבי דאין הלב דוה עליהם אבל פטר רחם מיהא הוו:
notes.en: And likewise one who miscarries [a form like] an animal, etc.: they do not count to exempt [the next son] from inheritance, since the heart does not grieve over them; but they do at least open the womb.

messages.text: The son is not exempted from the requirement of redemption from a priest unless his birth follows the birth of an animal that takes the form of a person.

notes.he: לא חשיב פטר רחם והבא אחריו בכור אף לכהן:
notes.en: Unless it has something of human form: [otherwise] it does not count as opening the womb, and the one who comes after it is a firstborn for the priest too.

notes.he: לעולם הוי נמי לכהן עד שיהא בו כנפל צורת אדם:
notes.en: And the Rabbis say: [the next son] is always a firstborn for the priest too, unless the miscarried fetus has a human form.

messages.text: In the case of a woman who miscarries a fetus in the form of a sandal fish or from whom an afterbirth or a gestational sac in which tissue developed emerged, or who delivered a fetus that emerged in pieces, the son who follows these is a firstborn with regard to inheritance but is not a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest.

notes.he: שאין לו צורת פנים:
notes.en: A sandal: which has no form of a face.

notes.he: שהרי אין שליא בלא ולד אלא שנימוח ומיהו פטר רחם הוי:
notes.en: Or an afterbirth: for there is no afterbirth without a fetus, only [the fetus] dissolved; and so it does count as opening the womb.

notes.he: עור ממש של ולד:
notes.en: Shafir [a gestational sac]: the actual skin of the fetus.

notes.he: מפרש במסכת נדה בהמפלת (נדה דף כה.) מהו ריקומו של שפיר:
notes.en: Merukam [in which tissue developed]: what the tissue of a shafir is, is explained in Tractate Niddah, chapter HaMappelet (Niddah 25a).

notes.he: אברים אברים ויצא כו' הוי פטר רחם אבל ראש מחותך לא פטר אם קדם אחיו ויצא קודם יציאת רוב אברי המחותך הני נמי בכור לכהן:
notes.en: In pieces: limb by limb, and [most of it] came out, etc.: this counts as opening the womb. But the head of a fetus in pieces does not exempt: if its brother came ahead and emerged before most of the limbs of the dismembered one came out, he too is a firstborn for the priest.

notes.he: בפרק המפלת (נדה כו.) מפרש סנדל דתנן גבי בכורות למאי הלכתא לבא אחריו וכו' וא"ת מה חידוש הוא הא בהדיא קתני לה הכא וי"ל דס"ד דבא אחריו דמתניתין דהכא היינו אותו שיולד בעיבור אחר ולא אותו שעם הסנדל דרגילות הוא שיולד קודם הסנדל ולהכי פריך למאי הלכתא דתיפוק לי שהרי בא אחר הולד שעם הסנדל דאין סנדל שאין עמו ולד ומפרש דלאותו ולד עצמו הנולד עם הסנדל אצטריך למתנייא דפעמים שהוא בא אחר הסנדל:
notes.en: One who miscarries a sandal, etc.: In chapter HaMappelet (Niddah 26a) [the Gemara] explains the sandal taught in [Tractate] Bekhorot: for what halakha [is it taught]? For the one who comes after it, etc. And if you ask: what novelty is that? It is taught explicitly here! One may answer: it entered [the Gemara’s] mind that “the one who comes after” in our mishna is the one born from another pregnancy, not the one [born] with the sandal, since [the twin] usually is born before the sandal. That is why it asks “for what halakha?”: let me derive it from the fact that he comes after the child who was with the sandal, as there is no sandal without a child with it. And it explains that it was needed to teach about that very child born with the sandal, since sometimes he comes after the sandal.

notes.he: פי' בקונטרס דרוב אברים מחותכים פוטרים את הרחם אבל ראש לא פטר במחותך והך מילתא פלוגתא דאמוראי היא בפרק המפלת (נדה דף כט.) דר' יוחנן סבר התם דאפי' מחותך הראש פוטר:
notes.en: And one that emerges in pieces: Rashi explained that most of the limbs of a fetus in pieces open the womb, but the head of a fetus in pieces does not. And this matter is a dispute of Amoraim in chapter HaMappelet (Niddah 29a), where Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that even in a fetus in pieces the head exempts.

notes.he: מפורש במסכת נדה:
notes.en: Sandal: explained in Tractate Niddah.

messages.text: In the case of a son born to one who did not have sons and he married a woman who had already given birth; or if he married a woman who gave birth when she was still a Canaanite maidservant and she was then emancipated; or one who gave birth when she was still a gentile and she then converted, and when the maidservant or the gentile came to join the Jewish people she gave birth to a male, that son is a firstborn with regard to inheritance but is not a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest.

notes.he: דלענין נחלה תליא מילתא באב דכתיב (דברים כ״א:י״ז) ראשית אונו ולענין כהן פטר רחם:
notes.en: Who had already given birth, etc.: for with regard to inheritance the matter depends on the father, as it is written “the first of his strength” (Deuteronomy 21:17); and with regard to the priest, on opening the womb.

notes.he: אפילו עודה שפחה בלידה ראשונה ונשתחררה עכשיו:
notes.en: While still a maidservant: even if she was still a maidservant at her first birth and has now been emancipated.

notes.he: ומשבחת ליד ישראל ילדה נמי הוי בכור לנחלה שהרי לזה לא היו בנים ולכהן לא דאינו פטר רחם:
notes.en: A gentile who converted: and once she came into the hands of Israel she gave birth. He too is a firstborn for inheritance, since this man had no sons; but not for the priest, since he is not the one who opened the womb.

notes.he: או ילדה עודה שפחה או ילדה עודה עובדת כוכבים ואח"כ נישאת לישראל שלא היו לו בנים בכור לנחלה. דהוי ראשית אונו:
notes.en: Or she gave birth while still a maidservant, or gave birth while still a gentile, and afterward married a Jew who had no sons: [the son is] a firstborn for inheritance, since he is “the first of his strength.”

messages.text: That son is a firstborn with regard to inheritance and with regard to redemption from a priest, as it is stated: “Whatever opens the womb among the children of Israel.” This indicates that the halakhic status of a child born to the mother is not that of one who opens the womb unless it opens the womb of a woman from the Jewish people.

verse.he: קַדֶּשׁ־לִי כׇל־בְּכוֹר פֶּטֶר כׇּל־רֶחֶם בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּאָדָם וּבַבְּהֵמָה לִי הוּא׃
verse.en: “Consecrate to Me every male first-born; human and animal, the first [male] issue of every womb among the Israelites is Mine.”

notes.he: דבנים הנולדו לה בהיותה עובדת כוכבים לא פטרי:
notes.en: For inheritance and for the priest: for the children born to her while she was a gentile do not exempt [him].

notes.he: כלומר דלעולם הוי נמי בכור לכהן הבא אחריו עד שיפטרו רחם מישראל של יהודית כלומר דהני דילדה בגיותה לא חשיבי למיפטריה מכהן לבא אחריו:
notes.en: Until they open the womb in Israel: that is, the one who comes after is always a firstborn for the priest too, unless they opened the womb of a Jewish woman in Israel; that is, those she bore while a gentile do not count to exempt the one who comes after from [the redemption paid to] the priest.

messages.text: In the case of one who had sons and married a woman who had not given birth; or if he married a woman who converted while she was pregnant, or a Canaanite maidservant who was emancipated while she was pregnant and she gave birth to a son, he is a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest, as he opened his mother’s womb, but he is not a firstborn with regard to inheritance, because he is not the firstborn of his father or because halakhically he has no father.

notes.he: ובעלה עמה וילדה הוי אותו ולד בכור לכהן דפטר רחם הוא בישראל ולא לנחלה דהורתו שלא בקדושה ולאו בר נחלה הוא וזרע מצרי רחמנא אפקריה דכתיב (יחזקאל כ״ג:כ׳) וזרמת סוסים זרמתם:
notes.en: Converted while pregnant: and her husband [converted] with her, and she gave birth. That child is a firstborn for the priest, since he opened the womb within Israel; but not for inheritance, since he was conceived not in sanctity and is not one who inherits [from his father]. And the Merciful One declared the seed of an Egyptian ownerless [that is, a gentile’s paternity does not count], as it is written: “whose issue is like the issue of horses” (Ezekiel 23:20).

notes.he: פי' בקונטרס ובעלה עמה וילדה הוי אותו ולד בכור לכהן דפטר רחם בישראל הוא ולא לנחלה דהורתו שלא בקדושה ולאו בר נחלה הוא דזרע מצרי רחמנא אפקריה דכתיב וזרמת סוסים זרמתם ובחנם פי' טעם זה דבלא"ה לאו בר נחלה הוא משום דגר שנתגייר כקטן שנולד דמי ואינו חשוב אביו ואע"ג דבעודו מצרי חשוב אביו גבי נחלה ולא אמרי' רחמנא אפקריה לענין זה לזרעיה דהא מצרי יורש אביו דבר תורה ומיהו בפרק נושאין על האנוסה (יבמות דף צח.) אמרינן הא דאמור רבנן אין אב למצרי לאו משום דשטופי בזימה ולא ידיע דהא שני אחין תאומים דטיפה אחת [היה] ונחלקה לשתים וקתני ואין חייבים משום אשת אח ש"מ אפקורי אפקריה רחמנא לזרעיה דמצרי דצריך לטעמא דאפקריה אע"ג דנתגיירו ולא סגי בטעמא דכקטן שנולד דמי ודבר תימה הוא וי"ל דאי לאו טעמא דאפקריה לזרעיה היה לנו לאסור למנסב נשי דהדדי משום דאתי לאחלופי בישראל והתם משמע דאפי' איסורא ליכא ואין חייבין לאו דוקא וגם היה לנו להצריך חליצה והתם קתני לא חולצין ולא מייבמין:
notes.en: Converted while pregnant: Rashi explained: and her husband with her, and she gave birth; that child is a firstborn for the priest, since he opened the womb within Israel, but not for inheritance, since he was conceived not in sanctity and is not one who inherits, as the Merciful One declared the seed of an Egyptian ownerless, as it is written: “whose issue is like the issue of horses.” He gave this reason needlessly, for even without it [the child] is not one who inherits, because a convert who has converted is like a newborn child and is not counted as [the son of] his father. [This is so] even though while he was an Egyptian [that is, a gentile] he was counted as his father’s [son] for inheritance, and we do not say that the Merciful One declared his seed ownerless in this respect, since an Egyptian inherits his father by Torah law. Yet in chapter Nose’in Al HaAnusa (Yevamot 98a) we say: what the Rabbis said, that an Egyptian has no father, is not because they are steeped in lewdness and [the father] is not known; for [it teaches about] two twin brothers, who were one drop split in two, and teaches that they are not liable on account of a brother’s wife. Learn from this that the Merciful One declared the seed of an Egyptian ownerless. So the reason “He declared it ownerless” is needed even though they converted, and the reason “like a newborn child” is not enough; and that is puzzling. One may answer: were it not for the reason that He declared his seed ownerless, we would forbid them to marry each other’s wives, lest they come to confuse it with [the case of] Jews; whereas there it implies that there is not even a prohibition, and “they are not liable” is not meant precisely. We would also require ḥalitza, whereas there it teaches that they neither perform ḥalitza nor enter levirate marriage.

notes.dh: או נתגיירה והיא מעוברת או נשתחררה והיא מעוברת
notes.he: האי ולד הוי בכור לכהן כיון שנולד ביהדות וחייב לפדות עצמו:
notes.en: Or she converted while pregnant, or was emancipated while pregnant: this child is a firstborn for the priest, since he was born in Judaism, and he is obligated to redeem himself.

messages.text: And likewise, if an Israelite woman and the daughter or wife of a priest, neither of whom had given birth yet, or an Israelite woman and the daughter or wife of a Levite, or an Israelite woman and a woman who had already given birth, all women whose sons do not require redemption from the priest, gave birth in the same place and it is uncertain which son was born to which mother;

notes.he: או בת ישראל מבכרת שילדה עם כהנת מבכרת ואין ידוע איזה ולד של ישראל:
notes.en: She and a priest’s wife: or an Israelite woman giving birth for the first time who gave birth together with a priest’s wife giving birth for the first time, and it is not known which child is the Israelite’s.

notes.he: דלויה נמי פטור בנה מחמש סלעים כדאמרן בפ"ק:
notes.en: Or she and a Levite woman: for the son of a Levite woman too is exempt from the five sela’im, as we said in the first chapter.

notes.he: ואין ידוע איזו בנה בכור לכהן. ורבותא קא משמע לן דבעלה של מבכרת חייב ה' סלעים לכהן דהבן זכר יש לו כל היכא דאיתיה ולא לנחלה דהא לא ידע בריה דמאן הוא:
notes.en: Or she and a woman who had already given birth: and it is not known whose son is the firstborn for the priest. And it teaches us a novelty: the husband of the first-time mother is obligated to give five sela’im to the priest, since he has a male son, wherever that son may be; but [the son is] not [a firstborn] for inheritance, since it is not known whose son he is.

messages.text: and likewise a woman who did not wait three months after the death of her husband and she married and gave birth, and it is unknown whether the child was born after a pregnancy of nine months and is the son of the first husband, or whether he was born after a pregnancy of seven months and is the son of the latter husband, in all these cases the child is a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest but is not a firstborn with regard to inheritance. Due to the uncertainty, he is unable to prove he is the firstborn of either father, and therefore he is not entitled to the double portion of the firstborn.

notes.he: נמי בכור לכהן והוא יפדה עצמו ולא לנחלה דהא לא ידע מאן ירית. ובגמ' פריך דאפילו פשוט נמי לא הוי:
notes.en: And likewise one who did not wait, etc.: he too is a firstborn for the priest, and he must redeem himself; but not for inheritance, since it is not known whom he inherits. And in the Gemara it objects that he is not even [counted as] an ordinary son.

notes.he: והך אשה שלא ילדה ואע"ג דילדה היא וכהנת ביחד ונתערבו ולדיהן או היא ולויה או היא ואשה שכבר ילדה ולא ידיע איזה הוא בכור שחייב לפדות ואפי' הכי הוי בכור לכהן וכן מי שלא שהתה כו':
notes.en: And this woman who had not given birth: even though she gave birth together with a priest’s wife and their babies were mixed up, or she and a Levite woman, or she and a woman who had already given birth, and it is not known which is the firstborn obligated in redemption, even so he is a firstborn for the priest. And likewise one who did not wait, etc.

messages.caption: The mishna’s four kinds of firstborn. Today’s daf gives the cases for the first two; the other two follow on 47b.

messages.text: Gemara

In a case where the head of a fetus emerged and then went back into the womb, the offspring is not considered to have been born and does not exempt the next fetus from the obligation of redemption of the firstborn, e.g., if its twin brother was born first. Shmuel says this halakha specifically in a case of miscarriage, i.e., where the fetus whose head emerged was a stillborn and the one that was eventually born first is a viable offspring. But in a case where both are viable offspring, the emergence of the head is considered birth.

notes.he: בן שמנה שהוציא ראשו חי והחזירו וקדמו אחיו ויצא הוי בכור לכהן שאין ראש הנפל פוטרו עד שיצא ראשו ורובו:
notes.en: GEMARA: The head does not exempt with nonviable fetuses: an eight-month-old that put out its head alive and drew it back, and its brother came ahead of it and was born: [the brother] is a firstborn for the priest, since the head of a nonviable fetus does not exempt him until its head and most [of its body] emerge.

notes.he: דנפל שלא כלו חדשיו אע"ג דיצא ראשו חי אינו פוטר את הבא אחריו מכהן:
notes.en: The head does not exempt with nonviable fetuses: for a nonviable fetus whose months were not complete, even though its head emerged alive, does not exempt the one who comes after it from [redemption by] the priest.

messages.text: What is the reason for Shmuel’s ruling? The verse states: “All in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life,” from which it is derived: Anywhere that one has the breath of the spirit of life, i.e., if it is viable, one goes by its nostrils, i.e., its head is considered significant. But with regard to another offspring, one that is not viable, its head is not considered significant.

verse.he: כֹּל אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁמַת־רוּחַ חַיִּים בְּאַפָּיו מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר בֶּחָרָבָה מֵתוּ׃
verse.en: All in whose nostrils was the merest breath of life, all that was on dry land, died.

notes.he: מי שהוא בן חיים הלך אחר אפיו דהיינו ראשו אבל אי לאו בר קיימא הוא לא חשיבי אפיה:
notes.en: The breath of life in its nostrils: for one that is viable, go by its nostrils, that is, its head. But if it is not viable, its nostrils do not count.

notes.dh: כל היכא דנשמת רוח חיים באפיו
notes.he: דבר קיימא הוא חשיב רישיה ליפטר לבא אחריו מכהן:
notes.en: Wherever the breath of the spirit of life is in its nostrils: since it is viable, its head counts to exempt the one who comes after it from [redemption by] the priest.

messages.text: We learned in the mishna: What is a firstborn with regard to inheritance but not with regard to redemption from a priest? It is a son who came after the miscarriage of an underdeveloped fetus, even where the head of the underdeveloped fetus emerged alive; and a fully developed nine-month-old fetus whose head emerged dead. Although the mishna addresses a nine-month-old fetus as well, in any event it teaches with regard to a miscarriage that its head exempts the offspring born after it.
messages.quote: who came after miscarriage, even where the head emerged alive

notes.he: נפל שיצא ראשו פוטר הבא אחריו מכהן:
notes.en: In any event it teaches: a nonviable fetus whose head emerged exempts the one who comes after it from [redemption by] the priest.

messages.text: What is the meaning of the term: Its head? It means its head and most of the body.
But if so, let the mishna teach: Most of it.
By right, the mishna should have taught: Most of it, but it did not do so, since in the latter clause of the mishna it needs to teach: A fully developed nine-month-old fetus whose head emerged dead.

notes.dh: איידי דבעי למתני סיפא בן ט' שיצא ראשו מת
notes.he: דלא מצי למיתני רובו בהדיא אע"ג דאיהו גופיה לא משמע אלא רובו ואהכי לא מצי למיתני בסיפא רובו משום דבעי למידק מינה טעמא דראשו מת הא ראשו חי אפי' בכור לנחלה לא הוי האחרון דראשו בן ט' חי ודאי הוי לידה ואי הוה תני רובו מת הוה משמע הא רובו חי לא הוי אחרון בכור אפי' לנחלה אבל אם יצא ראשו חי לא הוי משמע השתא דאחרון מפסיד הנחלה ואנן קיימין דראשו חי הוי כילוד משום הכי תנא ראשו ברישא ובסיפא ואע"ג דסיפא גופה דקתני ראשו מת לא הוי אלא ראשו ורובו:
notes.en: Since it needs to teach in the latter clause “a nine-month-old whose head emerged dead”: where it could not teach “most of it” explicitly, even though [the latter clause] itself means only most of it. It could not teach “most of it” in the latter clause because it wants an inference from it: the reason is that its head [emerged] dead, but if its head [emerged] alive, the later son is not a firstborn even for inheritance, since the head of a living nine-month-old is certainly a birth. Had it taught “most of it, dead”, the inference would be only that if most of it [emerged] alive the later son is not a firstborn even for inheritance; it would not be implied that he loses the inheritance if its head emerged alive, whereas we hold that [once] its head [emerged] alive, it is as if born. That is why it taught “its head” in the first clause and in the latter clause, even though the latter clause itself, which teaches “its head, dead”, means only its head and most [of its body].

notes.dh: ואיידי דבעי למיתני סיפא בן ט' כו'
notes.he: מגופה הוה מצי למימר דנקט ראשו משום דמשמע דוקא נפל הא בר קיימא הבא אחריו בכור לנחלה נמי לא הוי אלא סיפא דייק ליה בפשיטות טפי:
notes.en: And since it needs to teach in the latter clause a nine-month-old, etc.: from [the first clause] itself it could have said that it uses “its head” because that implies a nonviable fetus specifically, whereas after a viable one the one who comes after is not a firstborn even for inheritance; but from the latter clause it infers this more simply.

messages.text: It is inferred from there that the reason the subsequent son is the firstborn with regard to inheritance is that the head of this fetus emerged dead, but if it was a nine-month-old fetus whose head emerged alive, then the fetus that comes after it is not a firstborn with regard to inheritance either. Therefore, the tanna of the mishna taught in the first clause also that the head of a miscarriage exempts the subsequent son, to maintain stylistic uniformity.

And according to this interpretation, what is the mishna teaching us? Is it that once the offspring reached out its head from the womb it is considered a birth? We learn this in a mishna with regard to the fetus of an animal:

notes.he: מתני' אי אמרת בשלמא ראשו דוקא אשמעינן דראש הנפלים פוטרו ותנא סיפא אטו רישא אלא אי אמרת ראשו לאו דוקא ואין הראש פוטר בנפלים השתא לא אשמעינן מינה אלא דיוקא דדייקינן טעמא דראשו מת הא ראשו חי אפי' בכור לנחלה נמי לא הוי דכיון דאפיק בן ט' חי רישיה הואיל ולאו נפל הוא הוי לידה אפי' החזירו:
notes.en: And what is it teaching us: [that is,] the mishna. Granted, if you say “its head” is meant precisely, it teaches us that the head of nonviable fetuses exempts him, and it taught the latter clause on account of the first clause. But if you say “its head” is not meant precisely, and the head does not exempt with nonviable fetuses, then it teaches us only the inference we drew: the reason is that its head [emerged] dead, but if its head [emerged] alive, [the next son] is not a firstborn even for inheritance; for once a living nine-month-old put out its head, since it is not a nonviable fetus, it is a birth even if it drew it back.

notes.he: סיפא דתנא ראשו דכיון דמפיק רישיה כו':
notes.en: And what is it teaching us: [with] the latter clause, which teaches “its head”: that since it put out its head, etc.

messages.text: If a fetus reached out its head, although it returned the head, the halakhic status of that fetus is like that of a newborn, whose consumption is permitted only by its own slaughter.

notes.he: בפ' בהמה המקשה הוציא עובר ראשו בשעת שחיטת אמו הרי זה כילוד אפי' החזירו ואינו ניתר בשחיטת אמו:
notes.en: But we already learned it: in chapter Behema HaMaksha (Ḥullin 68a): if a fetus put out its head [while] its mother [was being slaughtered], it is as if born, even if it drew it back, and it is not made permitted by its mother’s slaughter.

notes.he: בבהמה המקשה הוציא ראשו אע"פ שהחזיר הרי זה כילוד ואין שחיטת אמו מטהרתו:
notes.en: We learned it: in Behema HaMaksha: if it put out its head, even though it drew it back, it is as if born, and its mother’s slaughter does not make it permitted.

messages.text: And if you would say that the mishna there teaches us this halakha with regard to animals, and the mishna here teaches us that the same halakha applies to a human, this does not resolve the difficulty.

Two rulings might be necessary with regard to people and animals: The reason is that the halakha of a human cannot be derived from that of an animal, as the animal has no concealed opening, i.e., the opening of an animal’s womb is not hidden. Consequently, one might have thought that only in the case of an animal is the emergence of the head considered a birth. By contrast, in humans, where the woman’s thighs conceal the opening of the womb and the emergence of the head alone is not noticeable, perhaps the emergence of the head is not considered a full-fledged birth.

notes.he: אין רחם שלה בין ירכותיה הלכך חשיב הראש לידה דבגלוי הוא אבל אשה דיריכים שלה מכסים את הרחם לא חשיב ראש לידה:
notes.en: An animal has no prozdor [concealed opening]: its womb is not between its thighs, so the head counts as a birth, since it is in the open. But with a woman, whose thighs cover the womb, the head does not count as a birth.

notes.dh: דאדם מבהמה לא יליף דלית לה פרוזדור
notes.he: האי פרוזדור דהכא ובריש בהמה המקשה (חולין דף סח.) ובשבת פ' א"ר עקיבא (דף פו:) שוים ולא הוי כי ההוא דפרק יוצא דופן (נדה דף מב:) דמכי הוציא ולד ראשו חוץ לפרוזדור הוי כילוד דאי בפרוזדור דהתם אמרינן הכא מה יכול להחזיק הפרוזדור לעכב הלידה כיון שהראש חוצה לו אלא פרוזדור דהתם הוא בית החיצון ופרוזדור דהכא הוא עובי הירכים שמכסים את הרחם שבין ירכים והוה אמינא דלא חשיב ראש לידה ביציאת הרחם ואין תימה על שהלשון שוה ואין פירושם שוה דכי ה"ג אשכחן לעיל בפ' הלוקח בהמה (בכורות דף כ.) דטינוף פוטר בבכורה דחשיב ולד ולא הוי כההיא טינוף דפ' המפלת (נדה דף כט.) דרוב היולדות מטנפות:
notes.en: A human cannot be derived from an animal, since it has no prozdor: the prozdor here, at the beginning of Behema HaMaksha (Ḥullin 68a), and in Shabbat, chapter Amar Rabbi Akiva (86b), are the same, and it is not like the one in chapter Yotzei Dofen (Niddah 42b), [where] once a fetus has put its head out beyond the prozdor it is as if born. For if it were the prozdor of that passage, what could the prozdor here do to hold back the birth, once the head is outside it? Rather, the prozdor there is the outer chamber, while the prozdor here is the thickness of the thighs that cover the womb between them; and I would have said that the head’s leaving the womb does not count as a birth. Nor is it surprising that the term is the same while its meaning is not, for we find the same above in chapter HaLoke’aḥ Behema (Bekhorot 20a): a tinnuf [a shapeless discharge] exempts from firstborn status, since it counts as a fetus, and that is not like the tinnuf in chapter HaMappelet (Niddah 29a), [where it says] most women in labor have a discharge.

notes.he: דבהמה כיון דלית לה פרוזדור לאלתר כי הוציא ראשו הוי כילוד אבל (אדם) אשה כיון דאית לה פרוזדור דמעכב אימא דלא ליהוי כילוד קמ"ל סיפא דמתניתין דהוי [כילוד] ואכתי אמאי איצטריך לסיפא דהכא למיתנא ראשו הא נמי תנינא דרוב ראשו הוי כילוד:
notes.en: For an animal, since it has no prozdor, as soon as it puts out its head it is as if born. But a woman, since she has a prozdor that holds [the birth] back, say it is not as if born; [so] the latter clause of our mishna teaches us that it is [as if born]. Still, why was the latter clause here needed to teach “its head”? We already learned that most of its head counts as born.

messages.text: Conversely, had this ruling been taught only with regard to humans, one would have said that the halakha of animals cannot be derived from that of a human because the countenance of a person’s face is significant, as people are created in the image of God. This is not so with regard to animals.
Even so, this does not resolve the difficulty: We learn that ruling with regard to people also, in a mishna:

notes.he: גבי אדם במסכת נדה מי שיצא רוב ראשו הוי ילוד דאפילו החזירו ולא נולד עד לאחר ק' ימים חשיב ילוד מיום ראשון וחשבינן לה ימי טומאה וטהרה מיום ראשון:
notes.en: We already learned this too: about a human, in Tractate Niddah: one whose head emerged for the most part counts as born. So even if it drew back and was not born until a hundred days later, it is considered born from the first day, and we count her days of impurity and purity from the first day.

messages.text: If the fetus emerged in the usual manner, head first, it is considered born only when most of its head emerges. And what is considered most of its head? It is from when its forehead emerges.

notes.he: לאפוקי היכא דיצא דרך מרגלותיו דודאי לא חשיב ילוד עד יציאת רובו:
notes.en: It emerged in its usual manner: excluding where it came out feet first, where it certainly does not count as born until most of it emerges.

notes.he: ראשו קודם:
notes.en: It emerged in its usual manner: its head first.

messages.text: Accordingly, there was no need for the mishna here to state the halakha with regard to the head of a nine-month-old fetus, and the mention of a head with regard to a miscarriage contradicts the opinion of Shmuel.

notes.he: דודאי ראשו דנפלים דמתני' דוקא:
notes.en: A refutation of Shmuel: since the “its head” said of nonviable fetuses in the mishna is certainly meant precisely.

notes.he: לא הוי מצי לאקשויי לשמואל מהא דתנן בפ' בהמה המקשה (חולין דף עז.) שליא שיצתה מקצתה אסורה באכילה דדייקינן נינה התם בדיש פירקין (דף סח.) דביציאת ראש הויא לידה מדאסרינן להו ביציאת מקצת דשמא הראש ישנו באותו מקצת דהיינו דוקא בבהמה אבל אדם לא שמעינן מהתם דהא דקתני סיפא כסימן ולד באשה כך סימן ולד בבהמה היינו לענין שליא דהויא סימן ולד ואין להקשות דבבהמה המקשה היכי דייק מינה דביציאת ראש הוי כילוד דלמא הא דאסורה משום דגזרינן מקצתה אטו רובא כדאמר בפ"ק דב"ק (דף יא.) דאם איתא דביציאת ראש לא הוי לידה לא היה ראוי לגזור כיון דבמקצת אי אפשר לבא בשום פעם לידי חשיבות לידה וא"ת כיון דאיתותב שמואל מאי האי דקאמר בפרק המפלת (נדה דף כו.) גבי הסנדל ולד דאית ליה חיותא מכי נפיק רישיה הויא ליה לידה סנדל עד דנפיק רובא בלאו טעמא דחיותא נמי הא אפילו מתים הראש פוטר וי"ל דחיותא לאו דוקא אלא ראוי לחיותא ואגב דנקט נמי התם לעיל האי לישנא ולד דאית ביה חיותא סריך ולא נפיק סנדל דלית ביה חיותא שריק ונפיק נקטיה נמי בתר הכי ויש ספרים דגרס התם ולד דאית ביה חיותא מכי נפיק רוביה סנדל עד דנפיק כוליה ויש לפרש דרוביה דקאמר היינו רובא דרישא ואית דגרם בהדיא הכא נפק רובא דרישא והא דאמרי' התם בפרק המפלת (נדה דף כט.) בשמעתין דיצא מחותך או מסורס [משיצא רובו ה"ז כילוד] הא כתקנו הראש פוטר ר' יוסי אומר משיצא כתקנו לחיים לא כמו שפירש רבינו חננאל דלחיים היינו בר קיימא דהא אפי' בנפלים הראש פוטר דאיתותב שמואל הכא אלא כמו שפירש שם בקונט' כתקנו לחיים שלם לאפוקי מחותך:
notes.en: In brief: [1] The Gemara could not have refuted Shmuel from the mishna in Behema HaMaksha (Ḥullin 77a), “an afterbirth that partly emerged is forbidden to eat,” from which the beginning of that chapter (Ḥullin 68a) infers that the emergence of the head is a birth, since the head may be in that part: that applies only to animals and says nothing about humans; the line there “as the sign of a fetus in a woman, so the sign of a fetus in an animal” concerns only the afterbirth as a sign of a fetus. [2] Nor can one object that Ḥullin’s inference fails because a part may be forbidden as a decree on account of most of it (as in Bava Kamma 11a): if the head’s emergence were not a birth, there would be no reason to decree, since a part could never amount to a birth. [3] And if you ask: since Shmuel is refuted, why does chapter HaMappelet (Niddah 26a) say, about the sandal, that a fetus with life in it counts as born once its head emerges, but a sandal not until most of it emerges, when even after dead ones the head exempts? Answer: “life” is not meant precisely but means fit for life, and the phrase follows the line just before it there, contrasting a living fetus that holds back with a sandal that has no life and slips out. Some books read there “a fetus with life, once most of it emerges; a sandal, until all of it emerges”, which may mean most of the head, and some read explicitly “most of the head”. [4] And the passage in HaMappelet (Niddah 29a), “if it emerged in pieces or reversed, [once most of it emerges it is as if born]; in its normal manner, the head exempts; Rabbi Yosei says: once it emerges in its normal manner for life”, is not as Rabbeinu Ḥananel explained, that “for life” means viable, since even with nonviable fetuses the head exempts, as Shmuel is refuted here; rather, as Rashi explained there, “in its normal manner for life” means whole, excluding one in pieces. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: אלמא דסיפא גופה לא איצטריך ליה למיתני לאשמועינן דראשו חשוב לידה ורישא אמאי תני ראשו אלא ודאי לאו משום סיפא קתני ולא רובו הוי אלא ראשו ממש וקתני פוטר אלמא הראש פוטר בנפלים ותיובתא דשמואל:
notes.en: Once its forehead emerges: evidently [the mishna] did not need the latter clause itself to teach us that its head counts as a birth. Then why does the first clause teach “its head”? Rather, it certainly does not teach it on account of the latter clause, and it does not mean most of it but its actual head, and it teaches that it exempts. Evidently the head exempts with nonviable fetuses, and this is a refutation of Shmuel.

messages.text: ✖ The refutation of the opinion of Shmuel is indeed a conclusive refutation.

The emergence of a forehead alone in the case of a person exempts, i.e., is considered a birth, in all cases, except with regard to inheritance. If a son reached out his head alone and then brought it back, after which his twin brother was born, the second brother is the firstborn with regard to inheritance.

notes.he: מצח:
notes.en: Paddaḥat: the forehead.

notes.he: דחשיב לידה מיציאת פדחת. ובכ"מ מפרש לקמיה:
notes.en: [Exempts] in all cases: it counts as a birth from the emergence of the forehead. And “in all cases” is explained below.

notes.he: דהבא אחריו בכור לנחלה אא"כ יצא פניו של ראשון:
notes.en: Except for inheritance: the one who comes after him is a firstborn for inheritance, unless the face of the first came out.

messages.text: What is the reason? The Merciful One states: “For he shall recognize the firstborn, the son of the hated, by giving him a double portion of all that he has,” and recognition is not attained by emergence of the forehead alone.

verse.he: כִּי אֶת־הַבְּכֹר בֶּן־הַשְּׂנוּאָה יַכִּיר לָתֶת לוֹ פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר־יִמָּצֵא לוֹ כִּי־הוּא רֵאשִׁית אֹנוֹ לוֹ מִשְׁפַּט הַבְּכֹרָה׃ {ס}
verse.en: Instead, he must accept the first-born, the son of the unloved one, and allot to him a double portion of all he possesses; since he is the first fruit of his vigor, the birthright is his due.

notes.he: והיכרא ליתא אלא בפרצוף פנים:
notes.en: As it is written “he shall recognize”: and recognition exists only with the countenance of the face.

notes.he: תימה בפ' עשרה יוחסין (קדושין דף עח:) ובפ' יש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קכז:) שדוחק לרבנן דרבי יהודה יכיר למה לי לימא דאיצטריך לכדדרשינן הכא דאפי' רבי יוחנן לא פליג דהא דקאמר אף לנחלה משום דקסבר דפדחת נמי הויא היכרא וגם דוחק ביש נוחלין (שם) לר"מ דאמר אדם מקנה כו' דאתא יכיר לנכסים שנפלו לו כשהוא גוסס וי"ל דהתם קשיא ליה לשון יכיר דמשמע שיש כח בהכרת האב:
notes.en: What is the reason? “He shall recognize” is written: It is puzzling: in chapter Asara Yuḥasin (Kiddushin 78b) and chapter Yesh Noḥalin (Bava Batra 127b) [the Gemara] strains [to explain], according to the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Yehuda, why “he shall recognize” is needed. Let it say it is needed for what we expound here! For even Rabbi Yoḥanan does not disagree [with this exposition]: he says “even for inheritance” only because he holds that the forehead too is a recognition. And [the Gemara] also strains in Yesh Noḥalin, according to Rabbi Meir, who says a person can transfer ownership [of what has not yet come into being], [explaining] that “he shall recognize” comes for property that fell to him while he was dying. One may answer that there [the Gemara] is troubled by the wording “he shall recognize”, which implies that there is power in the father’s recognition.

notes.he: משום דכתיב יכיר לו לתת לו פי שנים ובפדחת בלא פנים לא הוי היכר:
notes.en: What is the reason: because it is written “he shall recognize… by giving him a double portion,” and with the forehead without the face there is no recognition.

messages.text: Even with regard to inheritance the emergence of a forehead is sufficient.

notes.he: דפדחת נמי הוי היכרא:
notes.en: Even for inheritance: since the forehead too is a recognition.

messages.text: When Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says the emergence of a forehead alone in the case of a person exempts in all cases, what does this comprehensive phrase serve to include? It serves to include that which the Sages taught:

With regard to a female convert whose offspring reached out its forehead alone in her gentile state, and then she converted and gave birth to the entire child, one does not assign to her the days of ritual impurity and the days of ritual purity of a Jewish woman who gave birth. And likewise she does not bring the offering that a woman is obligated to sacrifice after giving birth, as the child is considered to have been born while the mother was still a gentile.

notes.he: עובדת כוכבים אינה מטמאה בנדה וזיבה ולידה:
notes.en: A gentile woman does not become impure with the impurity of menstruation, of a zava, or of childbirth.

notes.dh: לאתויי הא דת"ר גיורת שיצא פדחת ולדה כו'
notes.he: וא"ת מאי חידוש הוא זה בהך מילתא טפי משאר דברים דחשוב בהן כילוד כגון לזקוק אשת אחיו ליבום ולפטור מן היבום וההורגו חייב ושאר דברים השנויים בפ' יוצא דופן (נדה דף מג:) וי"ל דאיצטריך הכא לאשמועינן דס"ד אע"ג דיציאת הראש חשוב לידה מ"מ לידת שאר הגוף שיצא אחרי כן בקדושה חשוב כמו כן לידה וניתיב לה ימי טומאה וימי טהרה:
notes.en: To include what the Sages taught: a convert whose child put out its forehead, etc.: And if you ask: what novelty is there in this matter more than in the other matters in which [such a child] counts as born, such as binding his brother’s wife to levirate marriage, exempting from levirate marriage, one who kills him being liable, and the other matters taught in chapter Yotzei Dofen (Niddah 43b)? One may answer that it was needed here to teach us, since it would have entered our minds that although the emergence of the head counts as a birth, the birth of the rest of the body, which came out afterward in sanctity, also counts as a birth, and we would give her days of impurity and days of purity.

notes.he: קודם שיצאו הפנים ושאר הגוף אין נותנין לה ימי טומאה משום דהוצאת פדחת בגיותה הוי לידה ועובדת כוכבים לא מטמיא בלידה:
notes.en: And afterward she converted: before the face and the rest of the body emerged. One does not give her days of impurity, since the emergence of the forehead while she was a gentile counts as the birth, and a gentile woman does not become impure through childbirth.

messages.text: The Gemara raises an objection to the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan from a baraita:

When the verse states: “He shall recognize,” this is referring to the recognition of the face. And what exactly is the recognition of the face? It is recognizing the countenance of the face with the nose.

verse.he: כִּי אֶת־הַבְּכֹר בֶּן־הַשְּׂנוּאָה יַכִּיר לָתֶת לוֹ פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר־יִמָּצֵא לוֹ כִּי־הוּא רֵאשִׁית אֹנוֹ לוֹ מִשְׁפַּט הַבְּכֹרָה׃ {ס}
verse.en: Instead, he must accept the first-born, the son of the unloved one, and allot to him a double portion of all he possesses; since he is the first fruit of his vigor, the birthright is his due.

notes.he: דמי שהוכרו פניו ראשון הוי בכור לנחלה:
notes.en: This is recognition of the face: the one whose face was recognized first is the firstborn for inheritance.

notes.he: וקשיא לר' יוחנן:
notes.en: With the nose: and this is difficult for Rabbi Yoḥanan.

notes.he: וקשיא לר' יוחנן דאמר פדחת בלא חוטם פוטר אף לנחלה:
notes.en: With the nose: and this is difficult for Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said that the forehead without the nose exempts even for inheritance.

messages.text: This indicates that the forehead alone is insufficient.
Teach the baraita as saying: Up to, but not including, the nose.
messages.quote: the countenance of the face with the nose

notes.he: עד החוטם דהיינו פדחת לחודיה:
notes.en: Up to the nose: that is, the forehead alone.

messages.text: Come and hear a mishna:

One can testify that a man died, in order to permit his wife to remarry, only if he can attest to seeing the countenance of the face with the nose, as this allows one to identify the individual definitively.
Once again, one should teach: Up to, but not including, the nose.
messages.quote: the countenance of the face with the nose

messages.text: Come and hear another proof:

If people saw the forehead of a dead person without the countenance of the face, or the countenance of the face without the forehead, they cannot testify that he died and render his wife permitted to remarry until they see both the countenance of the face and the forehead, with the nose.

notes.he: להשיא את אשתו דשמא לאו זה הוא:
notes.en: One does not testify: to permit his wife to remarry, since perhaps it is not he.

messages.text: What is the verse from which it is derived? “The recognition of their countenance does witness against them,” and there is no recognition of a face without the nose.

verse.he: הַכָּרַת פְּנֵיהֶם עָנְתָה בָּם וְחַטָּאתָם כִּסְדֹם הִגִּידוּ לֹא כִחֵדוּ אוֹי לְנַפְשָׁם כִּי־גָמְלוּ לָהֶם רָעָה׃
verse.en:
Their partiality in judgment accuses them;
They avow their sins like Sodom,
They do not conceal them.
Woe to them! For ill
Have they served themselves.

notes.he: דהכרת פרצוף פניהם עדותן אלמא פרצוף פנים בעי. ופשטיה דקרא בנואפים כתיב הכרת פני הוולדות ענתה בנואפים שהקב"ה צר את הממזר בצורת פני המנאף:
notes.en: The recognition of their countenance does witness against them: the recognition of the countenance of their face is their testimony; evidently it requires the countenance of the face. And the plain sense of the verse is written about adulterers: the recognition of the children’s faces testifies against the adulterers, since the Holy One, blessed be He, forms the mamzer in the likeness of the adulterer’s face.

notes.dh: מאי קראה הכרת פניהם ענתה בם
notes.he: פירש בקונטרס דהכרת פרצוף פניהם עדותן הוא אלמא פרצוף פנים נמי בעי ותימה דביבמות (דף קכ. ושם ד"ה הכרת) מייתי קרא דהכרת פניהם ענתה בם משמע שיש דבר באדם שמכירים על ידו את הפנים והיינו פדחת דחוטם בכלל פרצוף פנים הוא והתם ביבמות (שם) בתר האי קרא מייתי עובדא דאבא בר מרתא דהוו מסקו ביה דבי ריש גלותא זוזי אייתי קירא דבק בבלייתא דבת אאפותיה חלף קמייהו ולא בשקרוה:
notes.en: What is the verse? “The recognition of their countenance does witness against them”: Rashi explained that the recognition of the countenance of their face is their testimony; evidently the countenance of the face is also required. And it is puzzling, for in Yevamot (120a) it cites the verse “The recognition of their countenance does witness against them”, implying that there is something in a person by which the face is recognized, and that is the forehead, since the nose is part of the countenance of the face. And there in Yevamot, after this verse, it brings the incident of Abba bar Marta, from whom the Exilarch’s household were trying to collect money: he took wax, stuck it on a rag, put it on his forehead, passed before them, and they did not recognize him.

messages.text: Testimony enabling a woman to remarry is different, as the Sages were stringent with regard to it. Therefore, they required greater proof than with regard to the halakhot of a firstborn.
And were the Sages stringent with regard to this testimony? But didn’t we learn in a mishna:
messages.quote: the Sages were stringent with regard to it

messages.text: The Sages established that they would allow a woman to marry again based on testimony that is generally not accepted, such as testimony based on hearsay, i.e., the testimony of one man which was heard from another man who saw her husband die, from a woman’s testimony, from a Canaanite slave’s testimony, or from a Canaanite maidservant’s testimony.

When the Sages were lenient it was with regard to the end of the testimony, i.e., to accept testimony that a husband had died even from individuals just mentioned. But the Sages were not lenient with regard to its beginning, i.e., the basic clarification of whether the witnesses properly identified the dead person when they saw him.

notes.he: לאחר שכוונו יפה בזה הקילו חכמים בסוף עדותן להחזיקן אפי' בעבד ושפחה:
notes.en: At its end: once [the witnesses] had identified him properly, the Sages were lenient at the end of their testimony, to accept them even from a slave or a maidservant.

notes.he: תחלת העדות דהיינו ראיית המת לא אקילו עד שיכירוהו יפה:
notes.en: But at the beginning: the beginning of the testimony, that is, seeing the dead man, they were not lenient, until they recognize him well.

notes.he: כי אקיל בסופה היכא דידעי דודאי מותרת דקא חזו דמת:
notes.en: When they were lenient at its end: where they know she is certainly permitted, since they saw that he died.

notes.he: בתחלה היכא דלא חזו דמת ולאסהודי עליה (דהוציא) הוא כדי להתירה לא סגיא אלא בפרצוף פנים עם החוטם:
notes.en: At the beginning: where they did not see that he died; to testify about him so as to permit her, nothing suffices but the countenance of the face with the nose.

messages.text: And if you wish, say instead that Rabbi Yoḥanan can resolve the difficulty as follows:
The second answer continues on 47a: “he shall recognize” for inheritance and the recognition of a husband’s face are separate matters.
